\section[glās]{\ml{ഗ്ലാസ്} (glās) — a glass}

\label{lesson:ML-C134-glass}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for ginger, then the Malayalam for sugar.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഗ്ലാസ്}}
\textbf{\ml{ഗ്ലാസ്}} (\emph{glās}) — \textquotedblleft{}a glass\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ml{ഒരു} \ml{ഗ്ലാസ്} \ml{വെള്ളം}} — \textquotedblleft{}a glass of water\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Something to drink from.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{glās}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{glās}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{oru glās veḷḷaṁ tarū}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for ginger, then the Malayalam for sugar, then say \emph{glās} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ഗ്ലാസ്} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A glass\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

What the tea goes in.
